question:
In the given reaction, which substance is insoluble?

2KBr+ Bal₂ → 2KI + BaBr₂
solution:
The correct answer is __**BaBr₂**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **BaBr₂** stands for Barium Bromide, which is a chemical compound composed of barium and bromine.
 
• In the above reaction, Barium Bromide is **insoluble in water** which is why it precipitates out of the solution.
 
• In the reaction, 2KBr + Bal₂ → 2KI + BaBr₂, BaBr₂ does not dissolve in water and remains as a solid.
 
• The formation of an insoluble precipitate like BaBr₂ is a common occurrence in double displacement reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solubility**

 
 
• Solubility is a chemical property referring to the ability of a given substance, the solute, to dissolve in a solvent.
 
• It is measured in terms of the maximum amount of solute dissolved in a solvent at equilibrium.
 
• Barium Bromide (BaBr₂) has low solubility in water, leading to its precipitation in the reaction.
 
 
 
• **Double Displacement Reaction**
 
 
• A double displacement reaction, also known as a metathesis reaction, occurs when parts of two ionic compounds are exchanged and make two new compounds.
 
• These reactions are generally written as AB + CD → AD + CB.
 
• In this particular reaction, KBr and Bal₂ exchange ions to form KI and BaBr₂.
 
 
 
• **Precipitation**
 
 
• Precipitation is the process of a substance being separated from a solution as a solid.
 
• In the reaction provided, BaBr₂ forms a solid precipitate because it is insoluble in water.
 
• Precipitation reactions are a type of double displacement reaction where an insoluble solid forms and separates from the solution.
